subject: Runbook dependency / SLA exception request — Koraxis private VPC
messages:
From: Samira Chowdhury <samira@koraxis.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@koraxis.ai>; secops@koraxis.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 12:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Request: runbook & SLA carveout for Koraxis private VPC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the Private deployment, our SecOps team has flagged the customer-managed border NATs and an MPLS tail at our edge as an operational dependency. We need a documented SLA exception / runbook that acknowledges the parts of the path under our control and details telemetry requirements and escalation steps.

Key asks:
- A short exception clause acknowledging Koraxis-managed edge components may cause latency spikes or transient unreachability (we need wording).
- Minimum telemetry/heartbeat endpoints Redwood needs (IP ranges, SNAT behavior) and preferred monitoring retention for traces during incidents.
- Evidence checklist for compliance audit (what logs and for how long).

I've attached a network diagram and added Procurement and SecOps to the thread. Could you share a draft exception and runbook snippet we can review by end of week?

Attachments: koraxis-infra-diagram.pdf (diagram)

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Infrastructure, Koraxis

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Chowdhury <samira@koraxis.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: runbook & SLA carveout for Koraxis private VPC

Samira — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. Looping in Vanessa (Customer Ops) and Karthik (SRE) so we can turn this into a short, audit-ready exception + runbook.

What we'll do next:
- Vanessa/Karthik: can you confirm the minimum observability we require from Koraxis (heartbeat endpoints, flow logs, and retention) and whether the proposed monitoring hooks are achievable?
- I'll prepare a one-page exception clause + a 2-step runbook (detection, validation, fallback) and share a draft by Tuesday.

Quick clarification for your SecOps: for telemetry we typically need (a) one synthetic /health endpoint (IPv4/IPv6 if available) with 30s–60s interval, (b) netflow or VPC flow logs exported to a collector we can read (s3/gcs/ftp), and (c) timestamps aligned to NTP within 2s for correlation. If any of these are a no-go, flag it and we'll propose mitigations.

Acceptance criteria for the exception: it must be scoped to customer-controlled edge components and include a remediation SLA window for when Redwood can assume responsibility (e.g., after failed customer failover).

Thanks — I'll circulate the draft after I sync with the team.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Request: runbook & SLA carveout for Koraxis private VPC — technical questions

Karthik / Naomi — forwarding Samira's diagram and Priyom's note. A few technical/legal points to validate before we send a proposed clause:

1) Telemetry / Evidence:   
   - We need 30 days of high-fidelity flow logs and 90 days of aggregated alert history for audits. Legal prefers 12 months for sampled telemetry, but we can push for 90 days with compensated evidence (packet captures) on request.
   - Does SRE require packet captures or just flow logs + synthetic traces?

2) Failover / Remediation window: 
   - Operationally, propose the clause say Redwood is not responsible for availability impacts originating upstream of the customer-managed edge; however, if Koraxis fails to enact their documented failover within X hours, Redwood will escalate and may trigger an assisted triage. Suggest X = 4 hours for major incidents.

3) Escalation path and access: 
   - For assisted triage, we need read-only access to flow logs or sip/registry records. Is read-only log sharing acceptable?

Karthik — can you confirm the minimum heartbeat cadence and whether a 60s synthetic check plus flow logs is sufficient for our incident detection? Naomi — if Legal agrees to the 90-day sampled telemetry + 12-month aggregate fallback language, we can present that with clear auditor notes.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Director, Customer Operations

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Chowdhury <samira@koraxis.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@koraxis.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: runbook & SLA carveout for Koraxis private VPC — draft attached

Hi Samira — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short draft exception and a 2-step runbook for assisted triage. Highlights / proposed language:

- Exception summary (proposed): "Koraxis operates customer-managed network components (edge NATs, MPLS tails, and on-prem load balancers). Redwood's availability and latency SLA excludes incidents where the root cause is demonstrated to originate in these customer-controlled components. During incidents, Redwood will provide assisted triage as described below but does not accept SLA credit for delays attributable to Koraxis-managed infrastructure."

- Observability requirements:
   * One synthetic /health endpoint monitored at 60s cadence (IPv4 or IPv6)
   * VPC/flow logs exported to a readable store (S3/GCS) with 30 days high-fidelity retention and 90 days aggregated alerts available for audit
   * Timestamps must be NTP-synced within 2s for correlation

- Assisted triage runbook (short):
   1) Detection: Redwood alerts on failed synthetic checks and abnormal flow log patterns.
   2) Validation & handback: Koraxis validates configuration and performs failover. If Koraxis does not complete the documented failover within 4 hours of first validation, Redwood will escalate and execute limited mitigation steps (read-only log access, connection-level debug) with Koraxis authorization.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-exception-draft.docx (proposed clause & runbook)

If this captures Koraxis' constraints, please confirm and we'll turn it into a contract appendix (legal review pending). If SecOps prefers a longer retention window for audits, list the required retention and we'll mark it as an exception to standard evidence.

Next step: Samira — can Procurement confirm if the proposed 4-hour assisted-failover window and read-only log-access are acceptable?

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
